verses.1: There, the powerful Ravana, along with his army, chose to reside as the sun was setting.
verses.2: As the pure moon, shining with the brilliance of a mountain, rose, a vast army equipped with diverse weapons lay asleep.
verses.3: But the mighty Ravana, seated on the mountain peak, beheld the beautiful features of that place, enhanced by trees illuminated by the moonlight.
verses.4: He saw the beauty created by radiant Karnikara forests, dense Kadamba groves, blooming lotus ponds, and the waters of the Mandakini river.
verses.5: The scene was further adorned by trees such as Champaka, Ashoka, Punnaga, Mandara, Mango, Patala, Lodhra, Priyangu, Arjuna, Ketaka, Tagara, Narikela, Priyala, and Panasa.
verses.6: In that forest region, illuminated by these and other trees like Aragvadha, Tamala, Priyala, and Bakula, Kinnaras, tormented by love, sang passionately with their sweet voices.
verses.7: Where they sang together in unison, their songs greatly increased the satisfaction of the mind.
verses.8: In the brightly lit forest interior, the Vidyadharas, intoxicated and with eyes red from drink, assembled with their women and indeed played and rejoiced.
verses.9: In Kubera's abode, a sweet sound was heard, like the ringing of bells, from the singing groups of Apsaras.
verses.10: The trees, swayed by the wind, released showers of flowers, as if perfuming that mountain with the fragrance of spring blossoms.
verses.11: A pleasant wind blew, carrying the abundant fragrance mixed with the pollen of spring flowers, thereby increasing Ravana's desire.
verses.12: The night had set in, enhanced by the melodious music, the profusion of flowers, the cool mountain breeze, and the rising of the moon.
verses.13: Ravana, despite his great might, had fallen under the sway of desire and repeatedly sighed deeply as he gazed at the moon.
verses.14: At that very moment, Rambha, the foremost of all Apsaras, appeared there, adorned with divine ornaments and divine flowers.
verses.15: Her body was smeared with divine sandalwood, her hair adorned with Mandara flowers, she had initiated a divine celebration, and her face shone like the full moon.
verses.16: She bore her hips, which were plump, charming to the eyes and mind, adorned with a girdle of bells, and an excellent offering for love.
verses.17: She was adorned with fresh, special marks made from flowers of all six seasons.
verses.18: She appeared as if another embodiment of beauty, splendor, radiance, intelligence, and modesty, covered in a blue garment resembling a water-laden cloud.
verses.19: Her face was like the moon, her beautiful eyebrows like bows, her thighs like elephant trunks, and her hands soft as new leaves; as she walked through the army, she was observed by Ravana.
verses.20: Having risen, Ravana, fallen under the sway of Cupid's arrows, seized her hand as she was going, and smiling, spoke to the blushing woman.
verses.21: "Where do you go, O lady of beautiful hips, what accomplishment do you seek for yourself, and whose time of prosperity is this, that he will enjoy you?"
verses.22: Who today will ever be satisfied with the essence of your face, fragrant like lotuses and water-lilies, which is like the essence of divine nectar?
verses.23: O timid one, whose chest will these two plump, beautiful, close-set breasts of yours, resembling golden pitchers, touch?
verses.24: Who today will ascend your broad hips, which resemble a golden disc, are adorned with golden chains, and are like heaven itself?
verses.25: Who is that man superior to me today, be it Indra, Vishnu, or the Ashvins, whom you, O timid one, would go to, leaving me behind, for that would not be proper?
verses.26: O broad-hipped one, you should rest on this beautiful rock surface.
verses.27: There is no lord in the three worlds other than me.
verses.28: Therefore, the ten-headed Ravana, bowing down with folded hands, begs you, "Worship me, for I am the lord of lords and the creator of the three worlds."
verses.29: Thus addressed, Rambha, trembling and with folded hands, replied, "Please have mercy; you should not speak such words, for you are indeed like an elder to me."
verses.30: You are indeed the one who should protect me from molestation by others, and by dharma, I am your daughter-in-law; I tell you this truth.
verses.31: Then Ravana spoke to her, who was standing with her face turned downwards towards his feet, having gotten goosebumps merely upon seeing him.
verses.32: Rambha replied to Ravana, saying, "If I were the wife of your son, then you would indeed be my father-in-law."
verses.33: O best of Rakshasas, I am rightfully the wife of your son, Nalakubara, who is dearer to your brother Vaishravana (Kubera) than life itself and is renowned in all three worlds.
verses.34: He (Nalakubara) is like a Brahmin by righteousness, a Kshatriya by valor, fire by his anger, and equal to the earth in patience.
verses.35: I am indeed promised to him, the son of a Lokapala, and all these ornaments I wear are for his sake.
verses.36: Thus, my affection is indeed for him alone, and not for anyone else.
verses.37: O King, destroyer of enemies, by that truth, you ought to release me.
verses.38: Indeed, that righteous one waits for me, very eager; you ought not to create an obstacle for your son in this matter, so release me.
verses.39: O best of Rakshasas, follow the path practiced by the good; you are indeed worthy of respect to me, and I am similarly to be protected by you.
verses.40: Thus addressed, Dashagriva replied as if humbly, saying that what she spoke about being a daughter-in-law and the custom of having one husband applies only to women with a single spouse, and that this custom of the divine world for gods is considered eternal.
verses.41: There is no single husband for Apsaras, nor is there a custom of having only one wife.
verses.42: Having said, "I am what you said, this is the rule among chaste wives," the demon Ravana, deeply engrossed in sensual pleasures, placed her on a rock surface and proceeded to engage in sexual union.
verses.43: Rambha, thus released, with her garlands and ornaments fallen, became agitated like a river churned by the sport of a lordly elephant.
verses.44: Her hair was disheveled and scattered, and her hands trembled like sprouts, resembling a flower-laden creeper shaken by the wind.
verses.45: Trembling, ashamed, and frightened, she approached Nalakubara with folded hands and fell at his feet.
verses.46: Seeing her in that state, the great-souled Nalakubara asked, "O gentle one, what is this, that you have fallen at my feet?"
verses.47: Trembling and sighing deeply, she, with folded hands, began to narrate everything to him exactly as it had happened.
verses.48: O god, this Dashagriva arrived here to go to heaven, and with the help of his army, he spent this night.
verses.49: O destroyer of enemies, I was seen by him while coming to your presence, and I was seized and asked by that Rakshasa, "Whose are you?"
verses.50: But I reported everything truly to him, yet his mind, overcome by lust and delusion, did not listen to my words.
verses.51: O god, O lord, despite being implored by me that I am your daughter-in-law, he disregarded all that and forcibly violated me.
verses.52: O virtuous and gentle one, you ought to forgive my offense, for indeed, the strength of a woman and a man is not equal.
verses.53: Having heard this, the son of Vaishravana (Kubera) became greatly enraged and, upon hearing of that extreme outrage, he entered into deep contemplation.
verses.54: Having understood that deed of his, the son of Vaishravana (Kubera) instantly, with eyes red from anger, took water in his hand.
verses.55: Having taken the water and performed the ritual purification, he then uttered a terrible curse upon the king of Rakshasas (Ravana).
verses.56: O auspicious one, because you were molested by him by force against your will, therefore he will not approach another young woman who is unwilling.
verses.57: When a lust-struck man violates an unwilling woman, his head will indeed shatter into seven pieces.
verses.58: Upon the utterance of that curse, which shone like a blazing fire, divine drums resounded, a shower of flowers fell from the sky, and all the gods, led by Brahma, were greatly delighted.
verses.59: Understanding the entire course of the world and the demon's impending death, the sages and ancestors indeed experienced unsurpassed joy.
verses.60: But having heard that terrifying, hair-raising curse, Dashagriva no longer desired sexual intimacy with unwilling women.
verses.61: All the chaste women who had been abducted by him attained great joy upon hearing that delightful curse uttered by Nalakubara. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षड्वविंशः सर्गः ।। 26 ।। Thus ends the twenty-sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
